assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 120,000 messages/s at peak: about 1,000,000 devices each reporting every 8 seconds, plus 6,000 rps of human traffic (dashboards and outbound commands). Telemetry is 94% of everything.

assumptions.subject: tsdb
assumptions.statement: visit_prob 0.01 on the ingest path is the BATCHING factor, and it is the single most important number in this design: the stream processor accumulates ~100 readings per device-partition before one write, so 112,800 readings/s becomes ~1,128 write ops/s. Remove the batching and the time-series store needs 100x the capacity. Dashboard queries hit it directly (40% miss the cache), and at 2,400 rps those range scans, not the writes, are most of its load.

assumptions.subject: gw
assumptions.statement: MQTT is a PERSISTENT-CONNECTION protocol: a real gateway holds ~1M open sockets, and connection count, not request rate, is what sizes it. The engine models arrival rate only, so this row is sized on messages/s and the socket-memory ceiling is NOT represented. Check it separately before trusting the instance count.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: The device shadow is written on every telemetry message and read by every dashboard and command, so the cache is the only component that sees 100% of system traffic. At 60% utilisation on 2 nodes it is the design's real availability risk: lose it and both ingest and the API degrade together.

assumptions.subject: proc
assumptions.statement: Stream processing is modelled as a request-serving fleet at ~5,000 msg/s per instance. Real stream processors are partition-parallel with checkpointing and rebalance pauses; the engine has no representation of either, so a rebalance storm (all consumers stalling at once) will not appear here.

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: 5 Kafka brokers at ~30,000 small messages/s each. Sized for both throughput and replication-factor-3 durability; the bus is also the ingest backpressure buffer, which is the reason it exists at all.

assumptions.subject: tsdb
assumptions.statement: 20 TB of time-series storage assumes a 90-day hot retention at ~100 bytes/reading after compression. Older data is assumed to be rolled to cold storage; that tier is not modelled.

_library.summary: Device telemetry pipeline: gateway to Kafka to stream processor, with batched time-series writes, a device-shadow cache and a dashboard/command API.
